title: Retrieve and verify data offline
author: Johan Larsson
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Retrieve and verify data offline}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

Datamonger can retrieve and decode data without contacting a registry or an
upstream provider. This example uses the five-row mixed CSV from the
[shared conformance corpus](https://github.com/jolars/datamonger/tree/main/tests/conformance),
which R, Python, and Julia use to check the same logical values and digest.

The package includes the corpus and its test registry. The setup copies their
known bytes into a fresh temporary cache. Every retrieval below uses
`offline = TRUE`, so a missing cache entry causes an error. In a research
workflow, populate your cache with the selected registry and artifacts before
disconnecting from the network.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(datamonger)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = FALSE, dev = "png")

fixtures <- system.file("extdata", "offline-conformance", package = "datamonger",
                        mustWork = TRUE)
selector <- jsonlite::fromJSON(file.path(fixtures, "registry", "selector.json"),
                              simplifyVector = FALSE)
cases <- jsonlite::fromJSON(file.path(fixtures, "conformance", "cases.json"),
                           simplifyVector = FALSE)
case <- cases$cases[[1L]]
stopifnot(identical(case$id, "delimited-mixed-csv"))

cache_dir <- tempfile("datamonger-offline-")
registry_dir <- file.path(cache_dir, "registries", "sha256")
object_dir <- file.path(cache_dir, "objects", "sha256")
dir.create(registry_dir, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(object_dir, recursive = TRUE)
index <- file.path(fixtures, "registry", "index.json")
payload <- file.path(fixtures, "conformance", case$input)
payload_sha256 <- digest::digest(file = payload, algo = "sha256")
stopifnot(
  identical(digest::digest(file = index, algo = "sha256"), selector$index_sha256),
  file.copy(index, file.path(registry_dir, selector$index_sha256)),
  file.copy(payload, file.path(object_dir, payload_sha256))
)
registry <- do.call(registry_selector, selector)
```

## Retrieve the verified artifact

[`fetch_artifact`] returns the cached CSV after checking its size and SHA-256
digest against the immutable registry record. The fully qualified reference
fixes the dataset source, name, and version.

```{r retrieve}
reference <- "conformance:mixed_csv@1"
artifact <- fetch_artifact(reference, registry = registry,
                           cache_dir = cache_dir, offline = TRUE)
artifact_sha256 <- digest::digest(file = artifact, algo = "sha256")
stopifnot(identical(artifact_sha256, payload_sha256))
artifact_sha256
```

## Decode the logical values

[`fetch_data`] also checks the registry's expected shape and canonical logical
digest. The decoder follows the declared column types, quoting, missing values,
and source row order rather than guessing them from the CSV.

```{r decode}
result <- fetch_data(reference, registry = registry, cache_dir = cache_dir,
                     offline = TRUE, return_info = TRUE)
data <- result$data
stopifnot(
  identical(dim(data), c(5L, 4L)),
  identical(data$measurement, c(1.5, -0.0, NA_real_, 20, 0)),
  identical(as.character(data$count), c("1", NA, "3", "4", "5")),
  identical(data$label, c("alpha", "quoted, value", 'says "hello"', NA, "omega")),
  identical(data$enabled, c(TRUE, FALSE, NA, TRUE, FALSE)),
  identical(result$info$verification, "decoded"),
  identical(result$info$canonical_form, cases$canonical_form),
  identical(result$info$canonical_digest, case$expected_sha256)
)
```

The decoded result has `r nrow(data)` rows and `r ncol(data)` columns. Missing
values remain missing, and the quoted comma and double quotes remain part of
their labels. The `count` column uses `datamonger_int64`, which stores exact
decimal strings so that large integers do not lose precision.

```{r values, results='asis'}
display <- data
display$count <- as.character(data$count)
knitr::kable(display, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Retain verification metadata

The artifact digest identifies the original bytes. The canonical digest
identifies their decoded logical values, including column types and missing
values. Retain both with the registry selector when recording an analysis.

```{r verification, results='asis'}
verification <- data.frame(
  Field = c("Dataset", "Registry release", "Verification", "Canonical form",
            "Registry SHA-256", "Artifact SHA-256", "Canonical SHA-256"),
  Value = c(result$info$dataset_id, result$info$registry_release,
            result$info$verification, result$info$canonical_form,
            result$info$registry_index_sha256, artifact_sha256,
            result$info$canonical_digest)
)
knitr::kable(verification, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Inspect the measurements

The third row has no measurement. Plotting the observed rows preserves their
source positions and makes the larger value in the fourth row visible.

```{r measurements, echo=FALSE, fig.width=6, fig.height=4, fig.cap='Four observed measurements; the third row is missing.', fig.alt='Rows one, two, four, and five have measurements 1.5, zero, 20, and zero. Row three is missing.'}
plot(seq_len(nrow(data)), data$measurement, pch = 19, col = "#2563eb",
     xlab = "Source row", ylab = "Measurement", ylim = c(-1, 21))
abline(h = 0, lty = 2, col = "gray50")
```

This small example verifies the complete path from cached artifact bytes to
decoded values, reproducibility metadata, and a rendered figure. It uses a
private temporary cache and removes that cache after execution.

```{r cleanup, include=FALSE}
unlink(cache_dir, recursive = TRUE)
```
